questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses **inversion** to emphasise the subject in a conditional clause?
options: If she had known the truth, she **would have left** immediately.
Had she known the truth, she **would have left** immediately.
She would have left immediately if she had known the truth.
She would have left immediately, had she known the truth.
questions.answer: Had she known the truth, she would have left immediately.

questions.question: Which sentence uses **cleft construction** to focus on the object of the verb?
options: It was **the book** that she had been waiting for all year.
The book she had been waiting for all year was **the one** she bought yesterday.
She bought **the book** that she had been waiting for all year.
It was **the book** she had been waiting for that she bought yesterday.
questions.answer: It was the book that she had been waiting for all year.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the **subjunctive** to express a hypothetical scenario involving a past event?
options: She insists that he **be** there on time.
She insists that he **was** there on time.
She insists that he **were** there on time.
She insists that he **be** there on time, but he didn’t arrive.
questions.answer: She insists that he **were** there on time.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates **ellipsis** in a complex sentence structure?
options: She didn’t tell anyone, **because she was afraid** of the consequences.
She was afraid of the consequences, **she didn’t tell anyone**.
She didn’t tell anyone; she was afraid of the consequences.
She told no one, **she feared** the consequences would follow.
questions.answer: She didn’t tell anyone, **because she was afraid** of the consequences.

questions.question: Which sentence uses **formal register** and a **complex conditional** to express a nuanced hypothetical scenario?
options: If you had taken my advice, you **wouldn’t have faced** this dilemma.
In the event that you had taken my advice, you might have avoided this dilemma.
Had you followed my advice, you **would have avoided** this dilemma entirely.
You should have listened; otherwise, you’d still be in this situation today.
questions.answer: In the event that you had taken my advice, you might have avoided this dilemma.
